correctness.rationale: PASS: In Z_(p)[[x]] the expansion (1-x)^p=1-x^p-p*sum_{1<=j<p}x^j/j modulo p^2, after substituting x^(2d+1) and dividing the two series, gives C_d(p)=1-p sum_{(2d+1)j<=dp, p|(2d+1)j} j^(-1) mod p^2. Nonexceptional primes make the sum empty. If p|(2d+1), the range is j<= (p-1)/2, yielding -H_{(p-1)/2}=(2^p-2)/p mod p by binomial expansion. Boundary d=0 and Wieferich collisions handled as congruences, not strict residue inequality. Independent exact sliding-window vs inclusion-exclusion coefficient calculations tested 85 (p,d) cases, 3<=p<=13, 0<=d<=16.
